articles.title: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU
articles.summary:
Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU

Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari has urged the US and Iran to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator.

Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office.

His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states.

Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

articles.title: Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says
articles.summary:
Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says

Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.

The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships.

The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said.

"The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices," one of the two officials said.

The decision to adopt the new strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ruling system, the officials said.

A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Iran had changed tactics in one significant way: after the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had started using unarmed spotters in small boats to identify potential targets, including US naval vessels, the official said.

In recent days, attacks on commercial ships still sailing through the strait have surged to their highest level since the war began, according to independent data.

Report by Reuters
